chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Playing in silent film background music as a boy
summary: At 12-13 he played violin with his father's band providing mood music on film sets.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: It would be interesting to find out what it is (inaudible). You've been, your sound, has been in the movies for I guess a long time. The first time must have been with "Check and Double Check," and since then --
Oh, I worked in silent pictures --
I worked in silent pictures, playing background music, when I was 12 or 13 years old, before sound pictures came in.
No, at the studios. If you don't understand what that's all about, I'll explain it to you.
Please, because I don't know about (inaudible).
They had what they called background music that they would play for the audience and the actors, which was mood music.

If they had some pathos or something that had to be brought out, you played music to put them into the feeling that they should have for this particular scene and I worked at that when I was in junior high school, 12, 13 years old, playing my violin.
Oh, yeah, I do remember now somebody told me about this, but I had forgotten.
It wasn't what they call sideline in these days where you mimic a person that is playing, but this was actually playing behind the scenes while a scene was being done in silent pictures.
That's interesting. So you did that and then when sound pictures came in, (inaudible)?
Then I started playing sound. Yes, well, --
